newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end slightly lower on position squaring.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end slightly lower on position squaring.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly lower on Friday due to position squaring ahead of the weekend, traders said.

"Position adjustment ahead of the weekend, and long liquidation due to the fact that the September failed to extend gains after rising above 127.00 earlier, dragged down JGBs," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
Revised industrial output data for June and Tokyo July department store sales data released in the afternoon were within expectations and had little impact on JGBs, traders said.
The September ended at 126.83, down slightly from Thursday's close of 126.97. Turnover was 28,955 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.085 percent as of 0632 GMT, up from Thursday's close of 2.075 percent.

The key JGB yield fell to an all-time low of 2.065 percent in morning trade. The fall in the key yield was triggered by dealers' short-covering of the September JGB futures contract ahead of a benchmark shift to the December contract expected later this month, traders said.
The surge in JGBs in the morning session was also due to demand for cash bonds, traders said.

"Investors were detected buying government-guaranteed bonds with a coupon rate of 2.4 percent this morning. As soon as some investor sold these bonds, others jumped in to buy them," a regional bank trader said.

Investors such as city banks, regional banks and investment trusts who have been hit with unrealised losses while holding these bonds are unloading some of their holdings now that the bonds are trading near par, the trader said.
Caution ahead of a 10-year JGB auction due later this month may also have prevented JGBs from extending gains after reaching the 127.00 plateau, a brokerage house trader said.

"Even if JGBs stay stuck at current levels, that would likely cause the coupon rate for the new 10-year JGB issue to be set at (a record-low) 2.3 percent. If further buying ensued such a possibility would increase," the trader said.
Traders said the Finance Ministry would probably hold an auction for 10-year JGBs on August 26, rather than on August 21, as some had speculated.
"I think MOF has a tendency to hold 10-year JGB auctions on Tuesday, so I think there is a greater likelihood that the auction will be on August 26," the brokerage house trader said.
Japan's industrial production in June fell a revised 3.2 percent from the previous month, compared with a preliminary estimate of a 3.1 percent fall, the Trade Ministry said on Friday.
Sales at Tokyo department stores slipped 5.7 percent in July compared with a year earlier to 231.6 billion yen, the Japan Department Stores Association said on Friday.

Earlier, the market had expected June industrial output data to be revised slightly downwards or remain unchanged from preliminary figures, while sales at Tokyo department stores had been expected to fall by about five percent, traders said.
